harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed the inventory application on node1 via httpd, serving it on TCP port 8181 while SELinux remains in enforcing mode (confirmed via correct http_port_t SELinux port labeling for 8181, not by disabling MAC). Verified reachability, persistence across a full node restart, and no AVC denials.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: CentOS Stream 10, SELinux enforcing (targeted policy), no httpd/inventory app present, port 8181 free
Installed httpd and policycoreutils-python-utils via dnf
Created inventory app content at /var/www/inventory/index.html
Configured /etc/httpd/conf.d/inventory.conf to Listen on 8181 and serve the inventory app as a VirtualHost
Added SELinux port context: semanage port -a -t http_port_t -p tcp 8181 (confirmed as local customization via semanage port -l -C), then restorecon on the docroot
Enabled and started httpd; confirmed active/enabled, port 8181 listening, HTTP 200 response with correct content, SELinux still Enforcing, no AVC denials in kernel log or audit log
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, machine-id, SELinux mode, httpd status, HTTP 200 check
Issued a self-acknowledging reboot (backgrounded systemctl reboot after ack) on node1
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned; confirmed changed boot_id proving an actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: SELinux Enforcing, httpd active+enabled, port 8181 listening, SELinux port context intact, HTTP 200 with correct inventory content

evidence.requirement: Inventory app served over TCP 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: Created inventory app + httpd vhost listening on 8181, started httpd, confirmed port listening and curl returned HTTP 200 with inventory content

evidence.requirement: SELinux remains enforcing while serving on non-standard port 8181 (MAC compliance, not bypass)
evidence.summary: Baseline getenforce=Enforcing; added proper SELinux port label (http_port_t) for tcp/8181 via semanage, confirmed as active local customization; no AVC denials found after service start; getenforce still Enforcing after httpd start
Captured boot_id a70d7f83-..., SELinux Enforcing, httpd active, curl HTTP 200 before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot (2s delayed) so the exec call acknowledged successfully before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out twice during reboot, then boot_id returned as 4452f6d6-... (different from baseline a70d7f83-...) with a fresh uptime -s, proving the node actually rebooted

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data on node1
evidence.summary: After restart: SELinux still Enforcing, httpd active and enabled (auto-started), port 8181 listening, SELinux port context for 8181 intact, curl returned HTTP 200 with the original inventory content intact

attempts.summary: Deployed the inventory application on node1 via httpd, serving it on TCP port 8181 while SELinux remains in enforcing mode (confirmed via correct http_port_t SELinux port labeling for 8181, not by disabling MAC). Verified reachability, persistence across a full node restart, and no AVC denials.
